messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Elevated 5xx rate and tail latency detected for embeddings-eu-prod at 2471010105. Paging oncall (maria).

maria: acked. jumping in. seeing large numbers of kernel compile retries and 5xx for embed requests. grabbing logs and perf counters.

eric: I deployed a small change to the routing heuristic last night but it was only to canary; will double-check canary vs prod traffic.

maria: canary looks fine, but prod is noisy. pulling traces for failing requests.

eng-oncall: tagging in. @maria paste one or two trace ids so I can hop onto the traces UI.

maria: trace ids: tri-11b, tri-22c, tri-33d. pattern: long KV cache eviction + repeated fallback to alternate model variant -> repeated JIT/compile. seen kernel-thrash messages.

noah: i'm noticing a surge of long-context requests (30k+ tokens) hitting shared eu pool. routing rules intended to send these to dedicated fallback are not consistently applying.

tess: on the admissions side i can apply a temporary limiter. propose 50% admission for new embedding calls to eu pool to allow backlog to drain.

maria: do it. also start redirecting any requests with context > 20k to us-east fallback (added latency but keeps availability).

lisa: comms — i'll craft a short initial status page message. want to call out region, impact, and mitigation in plain language.

statuspage-bot: Reminder: include "estimated next update" and whether dedicated/reserved capacity customers affected.

lisa: INITIAL DRAFT (pls review):
```
Initial (2471010123 UTC): We are investigating increased error rates and slow responses for embedding requests in the EU region. Impact: Customers using the shared EU embeddings pool may experience failed or delayed embedding calls. Mitigation: We have applied temporary admission limits on the EU embeddings pool and are routing very long-context requests to a fallback endpoint in US-East. Engineers are actively investigating the root cause. Next update: in 20-30 minutes or sooner.```

noah: add a short line: "Dedicated/reserved EU capacity customers likely unaffected unless explicitly routed to shared pool."

lisa: updated DRAFT. also adding "no data loss suspected" per infra.

eric: one more note from infra: the fallback routing may incur higher compute and per-request cost while active. we should call that out to set expectations.

lisa: final DRAFT before publish:
```
Initial (2471010123 UTC): We are investigating increased error rates and slow responses for embedding requests in the EU region. Impact: Customers using the shared EU embeddings pool may experience failed or delayed embedding calls. Dedicated/reserved EU capacity customers are likely unaffected unless their traffic is routed through the shared pool. Mitigation: We have applied temporary admission limits on the EU embeddings pool and are routing very long-context requests to a fallback endpoint in US-East (this may increase latency and per-request cost for affected calls). There is no indication of data loss at this time. Engineers are actively investigating the root cause. Next update: in 20-30 minutes or sooner.```

noah: approve. tess: please confirm limiter values and ETA for rollback.

tess: limiter applied: admission set to 50% for new requests; TTL for limiter will be reviewed every 15 minutes. tentative rollback ETA 60-120 minutes depending on backlog drain.

lisa: publishing now.

statuspage-bot: Publishing initial incident update: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2471010123 - posted by lisa.

lisa: posted. alerted CS and account teams. (reaction :white_check_mark:)

--- ~25 minutes later ---

maria: update: root cause in progress. We are seeing model-variant selection flip/flop when KV cache misses occur, leading to repeated kernel compile cycles. Working on a routing patch to stop variant cycling and flush bad cache entries.

eric: pushed a configuration change to disable automatic variant fallback cycling in eu routing service. also scheduled a cache flush for the affected shards.

lisa: DRAFT UPDATE 2:
```
Update (~+25m): Engineers have deployed a routing change to prevent repeated model-variant fallback loops and have flushed affected cache entries in the EU embeddings pool. Error rates are declining and latency is improving for most tenants. Temporary mitigations remain in place (admission limits and routing of very long-context requests to US-East). We will continue to monitor and will provide a resolution notice once stable.```

noah: add "Dedicated customers unaffected" line again.

lisa: updated and publishing now.

statuspage-bot: Publishing update: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2471010123 - posted by lisa.

tess: monitoring metrics 95th/99th latencies trending down; some in-flight long-context jobs still draining.

maria: running fleet health checks to ensure no residual compile thrash.

--- ~100 minutes after initial ---

eric: metrics steady for 40+ minutes, error rate within normal thresholds, tails back to baseline.

maria: removing admission limits and resuming normal routing for EU pool.

lisa: RESOLVED DRAFT (pls confirm):
```
Resolved: The elevated error rate and latency affecting embeddings in the EU region have been mitigated. Root cause: model-variant selection cycling on KV cache misses, which caused repeated kernel recompilations and increased load. Actions taken: routing change to prevent variant cycling, cache flushes, and temporary admission limits while the backlog drained. Impact: Some customers on the shared EU pool experienced failed or delayed embedding requests. Dedicated/reserved EU customers were likely unaffected. There is no indication of data loss. Current status: service performance has returned to normal. Post-incident follow-up: validate checksum/variant validation in deploy pipeline and add additional canary regen tests. If you continue to see issues, contact support.```

noah: looks good. add a short note: "timeline and RCA doc to follow in a separate postmortem."

lisa: added, publishing resolved now.

statuspage-bot: Publishing resolved notice: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2471010123 - posted by lisa.

maria: filing a follow-up RCA with timestamps and suggested tests. assigning action items to eng-runtime and deploy infra.

eng-oncall: will run a scheduled integrity sweep on kernel caches and add alerts to detect variant cycling earlier.

eric: will add a validation step in the routing deploy pipeline to catch checksum mismatches.

lisa: closing thread. thanks everyone. (reaction :party-popper:)
